clue.text: Material for the famous medium's ambiguous play ?

parts.note: Daniel Dunglas Home was the famous Victorian spiritualist medium; with the possessive 's he gives this piece
a pun is play on words with two meanings

explanation.surface: A celebrated spiritualist's play with a double meaning is the source of a writer's material.
explanation.walkthrough: D. D. Home was a celebrated nineteenth-century medium who claimed to levitate; his name plus the possessive S comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun is cloth woven at home, a kind of coarse fabric.

clue.text: Offended when removed from the board?

explanation.surface: Someone sulks after being voted off the company's board.
explanation.walkthrough: In draughts (checkers), a piece is huffed when it is taken off the board as a penalty for failing to make a capture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a huff is to take umbrage; in draughts, huffing is forfeiting a piece as a penalty.

clue.text: Such wet ground could spoil the coconuts

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
a coconut shy is the fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts

explanation.surface: Soggy earth might ruin the coconut crop.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game, throwing balls to knock coconuts off stands, so 'the coconuts' stands for SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshy land is boggy, waterlogged terrain.

clue.text: Unsuccessful theorist returns here, honest fellow

parts.note: square means fair and honest, as in a square deal
one can mean a person, as in 'one never knows'

explanation.surface: A failed thinker comes back to find a decent chap.
explanation.walkthrough: To go back to square one is to start again after a failed attempt, which is where a theorist whose theory collapsed must return.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'back to square one' names the starting point a failed effort must resume from.

clue.text: Not lost, without a doubt

parts.note: un- is the prefix meaning not
from the proverb 'he who hesitates is lost', so lost stands for hesitating

explanation.surface: Certainly not lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' equates the two words, so 'Not lost' becomes not hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without a doubt means acting with no pause or wavering.

clue.text: Greek setter got fed up with non-solvers!

definitions.text: Greek setter got fed up with non-solvers!

parts.words: Greek setter got fed up with non-solvers!
parts.note: the riddling monster of Thebes in Greek myth posed a puzzle and devoured travellers who failed to answer it; 'fed up' means ate

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler from Greece grows tired of people who can't crack the clues.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the Theban monster set a riddle and ate anyone who could not answer it.

clue.text: It's crystal-clear she had bagged the baby I.

explanation.surface: A character admits she put the infant in her bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Prism, in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, left the baby Jack in a handbag at Victoria Station.
explanation.definitionFit: A prism is a transparent crystal block that splits light; Miss Prism is the governess in Wilde's play who mislaid an infant in a handbag.

clue.text: Whisky? Include a quarter for him

definitions.text: Whisky? Include a quarter for him

parts.words: Whisky? Include a quarter for him
parts.note: a quarter is a compass point such as E, and in Ireland the spirit is spelt whiskey, with that extra letter included

explanation.surface: A drink is offered, and someone suggests adding a quarter measure for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish spell the spirit WHISKEY, so for him the word must include E, East being one quarter of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Ireland spells the spirit with an E, one of the four compass quarters.

clue.text: Old Greek cross no phone reconnected

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: a line reconnected is put back together differently, so the words no phone are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angry caller has no telephone until the line is restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconnected' rearranges NO PHONE into ENOPHON, which follows X.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenophon was an Athenian soldier and historian of the fourth century BC.

clue.text: Sullen traveller interjected a cry of pain

indicators.note: interjected means thrown in among, so the cry is placed inside the traveller

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger on a taxi or bus
ouch is what one exclaims when hurt

explanation.surface: A moody passenger blurted out a yelp when hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche, borrowed from French, means shy, sullen or unsociable.

clue.text: Small type of favourite

explanation.surface: A particular style of print chosen as the preferred one.
explanation.walkthrough: Minion is the old printers' name for a size of type of about seven points.
explanation.definitionFit: Minion is a small printing size; a minion was also a royal darling or servile pet.

clue.text: Musical drama surely not his by choice

definitions.text: Musical drama surely not his by choice

parts.words: Musical drama surely not his by choice
parts.note: the proverb says beggars can't be choosers, so a work owned by a beggar was hardly chosen

explanation.surface: Someone stuck with a musical show certainly didn't pick it himself.
explanation.walkthrough: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera is named for a beggar, and 'beggars can't be choosers', so it cannot be his by choice.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's ballad opera of 1728 is a famous musical stage work about thieves and highwaymen.

clue.text: Heavenly air found here, above the range

indicators.note: found here points to letters lying within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Clear mountain air is to be had up above the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'abovE THE Range'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether was the pure upper air of the heavens in old cosmology.

clue.text: Vessel in which I pass them, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of I pass them are one possible arrangement among many

explanation.surface: A ship on which I overtake them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I PASS THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamship is a vessel driven by steam engines.

clue.text: It goes to pieces played at home .

definitions.text: It goes to pieces played at home

parts.words: It goes to pieces played at home
parts.note: 'goes to pieces' reads as accompanies musical pieces, played in a small house in the country

explanation.surface: Something falls apart when it is performed in a home game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to pieces' seems to mean collapses, but it means takes part in musical pieces; a cottage is a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage piano is a small upright instrument made for modest homes.

clue.text: Arrest. Brook for imitation of Goldsmith's work

parts.note: to pinch is slang for to arrest
a beck is a northern English word for a stream

explanation.surface: A forger of Oliver Goldsmith's writing is caught near a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith suggests the author Oliver Goldsmith but means a worker in gold; pinchbeck is a copper-zinc alloy that imitates gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinchbeck is a cheap alloy made to look like gold, so it imitates a gold craftsman's product.

clue.text: Looking threatening when boat goes to fish

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone glares menacingly when a boat heads off to catch fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowering with a frown looks menacing.

clue.text: Give line, perhaps, to ensnare

indicators.note: perhaps tells the solver that give line is one possible order of these letters

explanation.surface: An angler gives out line, maybe, to hook a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GIVE LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to lure or entrap someone by flattery or deceit.

clue.text: … but this gives a great performance playing away

definitions.text: but this gives a great performance playing away

parts.words: but this gives a great performance playing away
parts.note: following the home instrument of the clue before, this one is played away from home in public halls, the largest of its kind

explanation.surface: A team's star player shines in an away fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 14 across: unlike the home model, this instrument performs away in concert halls, and 'great' hints at its size.
explanation.definitionFit: A concert grand is the largest piano, built for public performance.

clue.text: A way to overcome our enthusiasm

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overcome is to sit on top of, so the first pieces stand above the last

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A method for conquering our zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passionate eagerness or zeal.

clue.text: Black magic ?

parts.note: the sorcery of the Caribbean and West Africa, practised in Haiti

explanation.surface: Dark sorcery?
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion of Haiti associated with spells and witchcraft.

clue.text: Changed route, when? For what purpose?

indicators.note: changed tells the solver the letters of route and when are to be put in a different order

explanation.surface: A traveller whose route was altered asks when it happened, and why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' rearranges ROUTE WHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Whereunto is an archaic word asking to what end.

clue.text: Chain letters

parts.note: a chain of linked S-shaped pieces, the collar of the letter S worn as a badge of office

explanation.surface: Letters forwarded in a chain to many people.
explanation.walkthrough: The collar of SS is a chain of linked S-shapes worn by Lord Chief Justices and heralds.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter S written in the plural names links shaped like that letter, forming a chain or collar.

clue.text: Dumb Marxist!

parts.note: dumb here means mute, and the Marxist is one of the Marx Brothers comedy team rather than a communist

explanation.surface: A stupid communist!
explanation.walkthrough: The silent member of the Marx Brothers never spoke on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx brother who played the harp never spoke in his films.

clue.text: Take in what is said as a joke.

indicators.note: what is said tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: something said as a joke is said in jest

explanation.surface: Accept a remark that was only meant in fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to swallow food, absorbing it into the body.

clue.text: Breed of cattle note, for inclusion in herd

indicators.note: inclusion in means the letters are placed inside the word herd

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A farmer notes which breed of cattle to add to the herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford cattle are a red-and-white beef breed from western England.

clue.text: Rock sounds nice.

indicators.note: sounds tells us the next word gives the pronunciation only

parts.note: the word nice itself, as it is pronounced

explanation.surface: A stone that makes a pleasant noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic stone.

clue.text: Mixing jar a cook used for a greenhorn down under

indicators.note: mixing, as a cook stirs ingredients, says the letters of jar a cook are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A kitchen novice uses a jar for mixing ingredients in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixing' rearranges JAR A COOK. Down under means Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a jackaroo is a young trainee on a sheep or cattle station, a newcomer learning the ropes.
